title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from context, since the previous page is missing): X is a normal two-dimensional local scheme, presumably henselian or complete, with closed point x and residue field k. One should take k algebraically closed. U = X − {x} is the punctured spectrum, and f: X' → X is a resolution with X' regular. The text relies on a construction 'loc. cit.' (Grothendieck, or Lipman-style) that represents the Picard functor of U by a smooth group scheme of finite type over k, written Pic_U. This gives Pic(U) = Pic_U(k) (8.13).

The neutral component and component group then give an extension 0 → Pic(U)^0 → Pic(U) → NS(U) → 0 (8.14–8.15), where Pic(U)^0 is the k-points of a connected commutative algebraic group and NS(U) is the k-points of the étale quotient.

Concretely, Pic(U) = Pic(X')/⟨C_i⟩, where the C_i are the r irreducible components of the reduced exceptional fibre. Taking degrees on the C_i gives Pic(X') → Z^r. This map is surjective over a henselian base with algebraically closed residue field, and its kernel is the 'continuous' part. Hence NS(U) = coker(M: Z^r → Z^r), where M = (C_i·C_j) is the intersection matrix.

By Mumford [28] (Du Val/Mumford negativity), M is negative definite. So the cokernel is finite of order |det M|; it is the discriminant group of the lattice. Because M is symmetric, the discriminant group carries a canonical nondegenerate symmetric pairing with values in Q/Z: (a,b) ↦ a^t M^{-1} b mod Z. This yields an autoduality NS(U) × NS(U) → Q/Z (8.16), which Grothendieck says is independent of the chosen resolution. Over C this is the linking form on the torsion of H_1 of the link of the singularity.

The last paragraph begins the ℓ-adic analysis. For ℓ ≠ char k, the structure theory of connected commutative algebraic groups over k (Chevalley-type structure, cited as [9, exp. 4]) shows that Pic(U)^0 is ℓ-divisible. Thus the ℓ-primary torsion and the ℓ-adic completion of Pic(U) are governed by NS(U). This is presumably in preparation for computing the ℓ-part of the local Brauer group or local H^2/H^3 of U and relating it to the autoduality (8.16).

The 'next page' is an unrelated handwritten scratch sheet: computations with Lefschetz operators L, L' and truncated polynomial rings Z[L]/(L^4) for Poincaré–Hodge algebras. This fits the stated topic of the folder, cote 16.
errors: Implicit hypotheses are not stated on this page: k must be algebraically closed (or at least separably closed) and X henselian, for Pic(X') → Z^r to be surjective and for NS(U) = coker M to hold.

Minor imprecision: NS(U) is identified with coker M. Over C, the full H_1 of the link can have a free part when the exceptional curves have genus or cycles. The finite NS(U) corresponds to the discriminant group, which matches the torsion part relevant here. No actual error.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an algebraic account of the local Picard group of a surface singularity and its discriminant (linking) form, apparently a draft of material close to Brauer III or a local duality discussion. The content is standard and matches Mumford and Lipman. The algebraic, resolution-independent Q/Z self-duality of NS(U) over a general field k, written in 1966–67, slightly predates Lipman's 1969 treatment, but nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'Pic(U)o' in the last line should be Pic(U)^o (neutral component).
The typescript reads 'introddisant' and 'abso[l]ue' (typos corrected by hand); the intended words are 'introduisant' and 'absolue'.
Handwritten insertion '[28]' after MUMFORD and '[9, exp. 4]' at the bottom are correctly captured; 'symétrique' was struck in the line and re-added as a marginal insertion.
'lisse et' replaces the struck 'localement' in the first line, giving 'groupes lisses et de type fini' (smooth, not merely locally of finite type).
